highlight.title: MCP 2026-07-28 Release Candidate Ships With Stateless Core and Tasks Framework
highlight.summary: <cite index="1-3,1-6">MCP's largest revision since launch delivers a stateless protocol core, Extensions framework including server-rendered UIs through MCP Apps and long-running work through Tasks, plus authorization hardening aligned with OAuth and OpenID Connect.</cite> <cite index="1-17">This foundation is expected to support MCP's growth for a long time, providing stateless operation on commodity HTTP infrastructure and a lifecycle policy that lets implementers build knowing their work will keep working.</cite>

resources.title: Tool Search Solves MCP's Context Bloat Problem
resources.why_now: <cite index="22-8,22-13,22-14">Tool Search reduces MCP token overhead by 85% and allows Claude Code to dynamically load tools instead of flooding context with unused definitions, making large MCP setups practical for the first time.</cite>

resources.title: Is MCP Dead? Analyzing Context and Reliability Challenges
resources.why_now: <cite index="6-3,6-5">Recent criticism highlights MCP's core issues: excessive context consumption, low reliability, and overlap with existing CLI tools, though Claude Code's Tool Search update has reduced context bloat by over 85%.</cite>

resources.title: AI Coding Trends 2026: From Assistants to Autonomous Teams
resources.why_now: <cite index="11-23,11-24,11-28">The shift to long-running autonomous workflows represents the defining transformation of 2026, with agents now operating through execution loops for extended periods rather than responding to single prompts.</cite>

resources.title: Claude Code MCP Setup Guide: Tool Search and Scoping
resources.why_now: <cite index="29-12,29-13,29-16">Tool Search fundamentally changes MCP deployment patterns by providing on-demand tool discovery, enabling 85-95% context reduction and allowing more server connections without performance degradation.</cite>

claude_take: <cite index="10-17,10-18,10-19">MCP is positioned to become the backbone of context-aware, interconnected AI as it transitions from experimental protocol to production infrastructure standard backed by major cloud providers.</cite> <cite index="15-31,15-37,15-38">With Anthropic, Microsoft, Google and OpenAI all adopting MCP as the tool integration protocol, it's becoming the OAuth-equivalent for connecting AIs to third-party systems, with adoption exploding in 2026.</cite>
